Closing verification (sanctioned non-force path), main @9bdb22f5887. Ticked all 4 ACs; also linked the canonical duplicate.

DUPLICATE: this is the same report as 3a70-3ade-6673-4a91 (alias mellow-coke-veto, same title and body, still in_progress) — the id the landing commit e2b70821e95fef9af3afd2a7288445c189443371 ('fix: resolve three open bugs ... plan-review signature contract', #93) actually cites. Linked c494 -duplicates-> 3a70.

- AC1 (BLOCK emits no passing signed attestation): src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py:113-120 — sign_plan_review raises SigningError unless verdict == PASS and coverage carries no resolution_class. The BLOCK reuse path mirrors it at src/rebar/llm/plan_review/reuse.py:180 with {'signed': False, 'reason': 'BLOCK'}. The commit's own note is that this was never a code defect: the footgun is that the verdict JSON's 'signature' OBJECT is always present, so a presence/truthiness check misreads a BLOCK as signed; '.signed' is the boolean of record.
- AC2 (claim gate unsatisfiable off a BLOCK): tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py::test_block_verdict_cannot_satisfy_the_claim_gate — reviews to BLOCK, then rebar.claim raises with returncode 1 and the ticket stays open.
- AC3 (documented): docs/plan-review-gate.md sections 'What the signature field guarantees (read this before trusting it)' and 'Signing is the DEFAULT on a passing review' state exactly when a signature is emitted, the {signed: bool} shape, and the explicit warning to read signature.signed rather than the object's presence.
- AC4 (regression test both directions): test_block_verdict_carries_no_passing_signature (BLOCK -> signed False AND no HMAC event on the ticket) and test_pass_verdict_carries_a_passing_signature (attested PASS -> signed True).

Verified now: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_plan_review_gate.py -k 'block_verdict or pass_verdict' -q -> 3 passed.
